hook.text: Remote workers log 1.4 hours more per day on average than office workers, per Airtasker research.

buildup.text: The guilt of invisible work drives overcompensation. You work more to prove you're not slacking.

discovery.text: Always-on doesn't mean more productive. After 50 hours weekly, output per hour drops sharply.

twist.text: Your company benefits from your rest. Burned out employees make more errors and less creative decisions.

climax.text: Set a hard stop time. Close the laptop. Disable notifications. Protect your recovery like a work commitment.

punchline.text: Log off to stay sharp. Overwork degrades output.

quiz.question: Why do remote workers tend to work longer hours?
options: They have more work assigned to them
Guilt about invisible work drives overcompensation
Remote work is inherently less efficient
